## Dependencies and Open Questions

- The `get_booking_status` two-path implementation ships only after [support-agent-tms-access](../support-agent-tms-access/spec.md) #18 lands (the scope resolver that compares `customerNumber` values against the authenticated Clerk organisation). ([from plan](https://lore.gcp.re-cinq.com/repos/re-cinq/Otto/plans/b4b2026f-63ce-4f1a-80bb-7a971f01f47f#p_16440c47-81de-4897-903f-6c5849ff785c))
- FR-043 is amended in the same PR as the tool: the amendment and the implementation are not separate issues. ([from plan](https://lore.gcp.re-cinq.com/repos/re-cinq/Otto/plans/b4b2026f-63ce-4f1a-80bb-7a971f01f47f#p_5120844f-054d-47a8-8850-527628bb5a5f))
- **Open - whether a server-side fault should escalate.** FR-107 keys the card text on escalation, so the four kinds that are re:cinq's fault rather than the customer's — `unauthorized`, `forbidden`, `invalid_response` and `unexpected` — currently tell the customer to try again, which is honest but leaves no human informed. Whether they should carry a trigger instead is a decision for [support-agent-escalation](../support-agent-escalation/spec.md)'s trigger set, not this spec: the plan names only `tms_unavailable` and `tms_timeout`, and inventing four more triggers here would set escalation volume by accident. `rate_limited` and `network` are transient and belong on the retry text either way.
- SC-006's card-rate measurement is deferred until HAL Engine provides a tool-call log; building the log is a HAL Engine library concern, not this project's. The order of work for the delivery card implementation is: HAL Engine `delivery_card` entry kind first, then `bowman-ui` rendering, then the tool, so the frontend renders `delivery_card` before the backend sends it. ([from plan](https://lore.gcp.re-cinq.com/repos/re-cinq/Otto/plans/b4b2026f-63ce-4f1a-80bb-7a971f01f47f#p_ceacb3e3-d110-4079-adb3-fc1a349c9f4b), [from plan](https://lore.gcp.re-cinq.com/repos/re-cinq/Otto/plans/b4b2026f-63ce-4f1a-80bb-7a971f01f47f#q-review-c4103095463), [from plan](https://lore.gcp.re-cinq.com/repos/re-cinq/Otto/plans/b4b2026f-63ce-4f1a-80bb-7a971f01f47f#p_7d00ceff-92d5-41ae-a211-ee0da77c1455))
- re:cinq holds no OLT key yet (no `OLT_API_KEY` in Otto, no such secret in Secret Manager); the working key (KU-02) is still owed by OLT's product contact. The tool needs `orders:read` and `shipments:read`; when the key arrives, `GET /me` returns `key.scopes` and `manglendeScopes`, and a missing scope is a request to OLT (403 `MISSING_SCOPE`), not a code change. ([from plan](https://lore.gcp.re-cinq.com/repos/re-cinq/Otto/plans/b4b2026f-63ce-4f1a-80bb-7a971f01f47f#p_c8608878-2c25-418f-a02b-3e090afff8b5))
- Thumbs up/down feedback is stored server-side (SC-007) through the [support-agent-conversation-data](../support-agent-conversation-data/spec.md) mechanism, which is currently under development; the delivery card feature depends on that storage being present before SC-007 is measurable. ([from plan](https://lore.gcp.re-cinq.com/repos/re-cinq/Otto/plans/b4b2026f-63ce-4f1a-80bb-7a971f01f47f#p_43632b60-b5c2-4e27-93d1-078d3d93493f))
- Blocked on `KU-02` (#19): `KU-01` closed on 2026-08-21 with the endpoint paths in `api/tms-openapi.json`, but response field names are derived from examples, so the response mapping needs verification against a live key. `mapping.ts`'s guarded placeholder constants (FR-054, FR-055) mark what waits. Until the key arrives, the contract-drift job's live half (FR-037) is a no-op; it becomes meaningful at M3.
- Blocked on `KU-03` (#20): the ten questions, in Danish, are owed by OLT's product contact. The endpoint columns can be filled now; the rows wait on the questions.
- #19 still names `KU-01` in `mapping.ts` (FR-054) and in the contract document's marking (FR-064), and marks its fixtures `no-documentation-available` (FR-056), although its own blocked note says `KU-01` closed and the endpoints are documented in `api/tms-openapi.json`. The issue does not say whether those markers move to `KU-02` and the delivered document.
- FR-063's contract-document path sits under `specs/support-agent-tms-tool-contract/`, the per-ticket spec directory this feature spec replaces. Whether the document moves to `specs/support-agent-tms-tools/contracts/` needs one answer.
- CR-009 still needs one fact the issues do not give: who can read `re-cinq/Otto`.
- The fixture format deliberately departs from the org's one fixture-format decision, CFOAgent's hand-typed TypeScript fixtures: these fixtures are a verbatim record of third-party behaviour, not a team-authored expectation.
- On an exhausted tool budget, the final round's tool results are pushed onto `messages` but the loop exits without another provider call, so the TMS is queried and the model never sees the answer. CFOAgent answers the equivalent case with an explicit Danish message; HAL Engine emits nothing.
- The crash guard depends on `registerTools.ts` from [support-agent-tms-access](../support-agent-tms-access/spec.md) (#18) as the single registration site, on the oversight gate of [support-agent-human-oversight](../support-agent-human-oversight/spec.md) (#33) and its CI grep over `.register(`, on the audit sink of [support-agent-audit-trail](../support-agent-audit-trail/spec.md) (#34), and on the escalation recorder of [support-agent-escalation](../support-agent-escalation/spec.md) (#24).
- `out-of-scope-mutation` rows route to a human because the factory already refuses non-idempotent methods (CR-014) and the EU AI Act human-oversight control does not exist yet.
- `questions/known-unknowns.md` (FR-099) lives in the OLT job's planning files, not in `re-cinq/Otto`.
- Repo state when this spec was written (2026-09-11): `packages/` holds only `.gitkeep` and a README naming `@support-agent/tms-client` as the first tenant, so neither the client nor the harness exists. `.env.example` has no `TMS_*` variable. `apps/api/src/tools/` does not exist, the tool registry is empty, `config.ts` reads no `MAX_TOOL_ROUNDS`, no `docs/` directory exists, and neither the audit trail nor the escalation recorder is implemented.

## Out of Scope
</document>
<document source="specs/support-agent-escalation/spec.md" type="spec" relevance="0.99" tokens="1901">
## User Scenarios & Testing

### User Story 1 - A TMS outage hands the customer off (Priority: P1, #24)

A customer asks a question while the TMS is down. The tool call fails with `unavailable` or `timeout`. The agent records an escalation without the model having to do anything, and tells the customer in the same turn that OLT will make contact. The conversation stays usable.

**Why this priority:** An outage is the case where the agent is certain it cannot answer. Recording it must not depend on the model choosing to act.

**Independent Test:** Drive one turn through the engine with a mock provider that never calls `escalate_to_human`, against a TMS fixture that returns `unavailable`. Assert one escalation record exists and the turn ends with `stream_end`.

**Acceptance Scenarios:**

1. **Given** a TMS fixture returning `unavailable`, **When** the customer sends a question, **Then** one escalation record exists and the model made no `escalate_to_human` call.
2. **Given** a TMS fixture returning `not_found`, **When** the customer sends a question, **Then** no escalation record exists.
3. **Given** a TMS outage, **When** the turn ends, **Then** an assistant entry is committed, `stream_end` is sent, and the customer can send another message.

### User Story 2 - The customer asks for a human (Priority: P1, #24)

A customer asks to speak to a person, or asks something no tool covers. The model calls `escalate_to_human` with a reason category, and an escalation is recorded.

**Why this priority:** It is the model-mediated half of the requirement. Without it, a model can promise a transfer while no record exists.

**Independent Test:** Drive a turn where the mock provider calls `escalate_to_human` with `customer_asked_for_human`, and assert one record. Drive a second turn whose assistant text claims a transfer while no trigger fires, and assert zero records.

**Acceptance Scenarios:**

1. **Given** a mock provider calling `escalate_to_human` with a valid `reason_category`, **When** the turn runs, **Then** one escalation record exists.
2. **Given** a call to `escalate_to_human` with an invalid `reason_category`, **When** the turn runs, **Then** the model receives a readable tool result instead of a thrown error, and the turn ends with `stream_end`.
3. **Given** assistant text that claims a transfer while no trigger fired, **When** the turn ends, **Then** no escalation record exists.

### User Story 3 - The customer is told when the tool budget runs out (Priority: P1, #151)

A customer asks a question that makes the model keep requesting tools until the budget runs out. Instead of an empty bubble, the assistant replies with one Danish sentence that promises nothing it cannot keep, and an escalation is recorded. A broken hook fragment on this path does not break the turn.

**Why this priority:** An empty reply is the worst outcome for a support channel, and this is the only turn ending with no owner.

**Independent Test:** Run the engine with `maxToolRounds: 2` and a stub that always requests tools. Assert one escalation document containing `tool_budget_exhausted` and the sentence in the committed assistant entry. Separately, compose a rejecting fragment ahead of the budget fragment and assert the terminal frame and the log.

**Acceptance Scenarios:**

1. **Given** a stub that always requests tools and `maxToolRounds: 2`, **When** the turn runs, **Then** exactly one document in `escalations` contains `tool_budget_exhausted`.
2. **Given** a turn that ends normally (`tool_use`, then `end_turn`), **When** it completes, **Then** no escalation record is written and the fragment is called zero times.
3. **Given** a first fragment whose `onToolBudgetExhausted` rejects, **When** the budget runs out, **Then** the next fragment runs, the terminal frame is `stream_end`, and exactly one `log.error` is emitted.

### User Story 4 - A provider outage leaves a callback record (Priority: P1, #178)

A customer asks a question while the model provider is down. After retries and failover have both failed, the customer sees the existing Danish error notice, and one escalation record for the conversation exists. A primary that fails over to a working fallback leaves no record.

**Why this priority:** It is the one failure mode that otherwise leaves no trace, while being the clearest case of the agent not being able to answer. A record means a customer is owed a callback; anything else is noise for OLT.

**Independent Test:** Run a turn on the real engine with a provider that rejects with an `AIError`. Assert one escalation document with `model_call_failed`, zero TMS calls, and that the `AIError` still reaches the caller. Then configure a failing primary and a working fallback and count documents.

**Acceptance Scenarios:**

1. **Given** a provider rejecting with an `AIError`, **When** the turn runs, **Then** exactly one escalation document contains `model_call_failed`, with zero TMS transport calls and no `escalate_to_human` call, and the caller still receives the `AIError`.
2. **Given** the same turn, **When** the collections are joined on session id, **Then** an audit row with `outcome: 'error'` and the matching error code sits beside the escalation pointer.
3. **Given** a primary that fails over successfully, **When** the turn completes, **Then** zero escalation documents exist.
4. **Given** a provider rejecting with a plain non-`Error` object, **When** the turn runs, **Then** zero documents exist, and a test pins this as the known upstream limit.

### User Story 5 - Repeated failures in one conversation make one record (Priority: P2, #24, #39, #151, #178)

A TMS outage fails every tool call in a conversation, and the customer tries three times. OLT gets one escalation for that conversation, listing each trigger, rather than one per failed message. Once a record has been delivered, a later trigger opens a new one.

**Why this priority:** One customer is owed one callback. Duplicate records would multiply the follow-up work.

**Independent Test:** Run three failing turns in one session and a fourth in another session, then count documents and `triggers` entries.

**Acceptance Scenarios:**

1. **Given** three failing turns in one session with no worker tick between them, **When** each flushes, **Then** exactly one document exists with three entries in its `triggers` array.
2. **Given** a further failing turn in a different session, **When** it flushes, **Then** a second document exists.
3. **Given** a TMS call that returned `503` and a budget that then ran out, **When** the turn flushes, **Then** exactly one document's `triggers` contains both `tms_unavailable` and `tool_budget_exhausted`.
4. **Given** a record whose `delivery.state` is `delivered`, **When** a new trigger arrives in the same session, **Then** a second document is opened and a second POST follows.

### User Story 6 - OLT's webhook is told about an escalation (Priority: P2, #39, #196)

A conversation escalates. After the turn ends, the worker POSTs a small pointer payload to OLT's configured webhook. The customer's turn does not wait for it. When the deployment has a view base URL configured, the payload also carries a link to the conversation.

**Why this priority:** It is the first time an escalation reaches anyone outside the database. It waits on `KU-14` for a real destination.

**Independent Test:** Flush one escalation, tick the worker against a fixture server, and compare the received body with the payload using `toEqual`, once with `CONVERSATION_VIEW_BASE_URL` unset and once with it set.

**Acceptance Scenarios:**
</document>

<document source="support-conversation-data-flow-record" type="memory" tokens="389">
**support-conversation-data-flow-record** (memory): ## Support Conversation Data Flow Record

Data flow record for the OLT support agent conversation data, per GDPR Article 30.

### Escalation hop (updated by issue #24)

**Previous status:** unmapped destination — the escalation hand-off was listed as a destination with no named store and no retention period.

**Current status (as of #24):** named store with retention period.

- **Store:** `escalations` collection in MongoDB (same instance as `conversations`)
- **Fields:** `sessionId`, `userId`, `trigger`, `occurredAt`, `updatedAt` — pointer fields only, no conversation content
- **Retention period:** same period as the `conversations` collection (set by the data-flow record; this issue does not decide the period)
- **Recipient:** undecided — KU-14 (owner: OLT product contact) determines where the escalation lands; no human is notified by this issue
- **Region:** follows the `conversations` collection's region (decided by `support-agent-deployment` #27)
- **GDPR basis:** same processing basis as the conversation itself (Article 6(1)(b) — performance of contract with the booking customer)
- **Retention sweep:** covered by `support-agent-conversation-persistence` (#23)'s sweep with the same period (CR-002)
- **Erasure:** erasing a conversation by `sessionId` erases its escalation record in the same operation (CR-004)

The notification hop (delivery of the escalation pointer to a configured destination) is a separate data flow added by issue #39 once KU-14 decides the destination.
</document>

**dod/otto-171-prompt-mask-blocked** (memory): DoD triage for re-cinq/Otto#171 (Give the support agent's prompt mask its OLT rule set) => changes_requested / Lore-Dod-Blocked. Branch lore/implementation-loop/issue-171, was level with origin/main (0/0). Committed only .lore/dod.md recording the block (no tests).

WHY BLOCKED (verified this run, not just memory):
1. G87 gate is OPEN. The ticket header AND specs/support-agent-prompt-and-model/spec.md (issue map L22, blocked row L12, dependencies L326) all mark #171 "Blocked: conditional on #31's transfer assessment (G87, G101)": build ONLY IF Lore's gdpr-cross-border-transfer-basis (#31) Transfer Impact Assessment adopts pseudonymisation as a supplementary measure; if it concludes `no transfer` or picks other measures, #171 is CLOSED UNBUILT. #31 is a Lore-owned issue, external to Otto; no spec/memory/commit shows it concluded. Building now risks building an issue that should be closed unbuilt.
2. Nothing resolved on base: origin/main has no apps/api/src/privacy/, no privacy.mask on the createHalEngine call in server.ts, no specs/support-agent-prompt-mask-rules/spec.md. So NOT Lore-Dod-Resolved.
3. The mechanism it builds on is itself gated. PromptMask/withMask/MaskBinding come from HAL Engine hal-engine-prompt-mask (#127), which spec L326 says is conditional on the SAME terms. apps/api/package.json pins @re-cinq/hal-engine ^0.2.0 (lockfile resolves 0.2.0). So tests through the real engine (FR-031 privacy.mask, FR-032 no signerName to provider, FR-050 round trip) would fail because createHalEngine does not accept privacy.mask / PromptMask not importable — a reason the ticket never states (it asserts "the engine already accepts a PromptMask"). Red for the wrong reason != DoD.
4. G101: FR-034 needs every maskCategories.ts row to name its endpoint, consuming #6's data-category list, which G101 records as having "no citable form."

<document source="specs/support-agent-escalation/spec.md" type="spec" relevance="0.99" tokens="1901">
## User Scenarios & Testing

### User Story 1 - A TMS outage hands the customer off (Priority: P1, #24)

A customer asks a question while the TMS is down. The tool call fails with `unavailable` or `timeout`. The agent records an escalation without the model having to do anything, and tells the customer in the same turn that OLT will make contact. The conversation stays usable.

**Why this priority:** An outage is the case where the agent is certain it cannot answer. Recording it must not depend on the model choosing to act.

**Independent Test:** Drive one turn through the engine with a mock provider that never calls `escalate_to_human`, against a TMS fixture that returns `unavailable`. Assert one escalation record exists and the turn ends with `stream_end`.

**Acceptance Scenarios:**

1. **Given** a TMS fixture returning `unavailable`, **When** the customer sends a question, **Then** one escalation record exists and the model made no `escalate_to_human` call.
2. **Given** a TMS fixture returning `not_found`, **When** the customer sends a question, **Then** no escalation record exists.
3. **Given** a TMS outage, **When** the turn ends, **Then** an assistant entry is committed, `stream_end` is sent, and the customer can send another message.

### User Story 2 - The customer asks for a human (Priority: P1, #24)

A customer asks to speak to a person, or asks something no tool covers. The model calls `escalate_to_human` with a reason category, and an escalation is recorded.

**Why this priority:** It is the model-mediated half of the requirement. Without it, a model can promise a transfer while no record exists.

**Independent Test:** Drive a turn where the mock provider calls `escalate_to_human` with `customer_asked_for_human`, and assert one record. Drive a second turn whose assistant text claims a transfer while no trigger fires, and assert zero records.

**Acceptance Scenarios:**

1. **Given** a mock provider calling `escalate_to_human` with a valid `reason_category`, **When** the turn runs, **Then** one escalation record exists.
2. **Given** a call to `escalate_to_human` with an invalid `reason_category`, **When** the turn runs, **Then** the model receives a readable tool result instead of a thrown error, and the turn ends with `stream_end`.
3. **Given** assistant text that claims a transfer while no trigger fired, **When** the turn ends, **Then** no escalation record exists.

### User Story 3 - The customer is told when the tool budget runs out (Priority: P1, #151)

A customer asks a question that makes the model keep requesting tools until the budget runs out. Instead of an empty bubble, the assistant replies with one Danish sentence that promises nothing it cannot keep, and an escalation is recorded. A broken hook fragment on this path does not break the turn.

**Why this priority:** An empty reply is the worst outcome for a support channel, and this is the only turn ending with no owner.

**Independent Test:** Run the engine with `maxToolRounds: 2` and a stub that always requests tools. Assert one escalation document containing `tool_budget_exhausted` and the sentence in the committed assistant entry. Separately, compose a rejecting fragment ahead of the budget fragment and assert the terminal frame and the log.

**Acceptance Scenarios:**

1. **Given** a stub that always requests tools and `maxToolRounds: 2`, **When** the turn runs, **Then** exactly one document in `escalations` contains `tool_budget_exhausted`.
2. **Given** a turn that ends normally (`tool_use`, then `end_turn`), **When** it completes, **Then** no escalation record is written and the fragment is called zero times.
3. **Given** a first fragment whose `onToolBudgetExhausted` rejects, **When** the budget runs out, **Then** the next fragment runs, the terminal frame is `stream_end`, and exactly one `log.error` is emitted.

### User Story 4 - A provider outage leaves a callback record (Priority: P1, #178)

A customer asks a question while the model provider is down. After retries and failover have both failed, the customer sees the existing Danish error notice, and one escalation record for the conversation exists. A primary that fails over to a working fallback leaves no record.

**Why this priority:** It is the one failure mode that otherwise leaves no trace, while being the clearest case of the agent not being able to answer. A record means a customer is owed a callback; anything else is noise for OLT.

**Independent Test:** Run a turn on the real engine with a provider that rejects with an `AIError`. Assert one escalation document with `model_call_failed`, zero TMS calls, and that the `AIError` still reaches the caller. Then configure a failing primary and a working fallback and count documents.

**Acceptance Scenarios:**

1. **Given** a provider rejecting with an `AIError`, **When** the turn runs, **Then** exactly one escalation document contains `model_call_failed`, with zero TMS transport calls and no `escalate_to_human` call, and the caller still receives the `AIError`.
2. **Given** the same turn, **When** the collections are joined on session id, **Then** an audit row with `outcome: 'error'` and the matching error code sits beside the escalation pointer.
3. **Given** a primary that fails over successfully, **When** the turn completes, **Then** zero escalation documents exist.
4. **Given** a provider rejecting with a plain non-`Error` object, **When** the turn runs, **Then** zero documents exist, and a test pins this as the known upstream limit.

### User Story 5 - Repeated failures in one conversation make one record (Priority: P2, #24, #39, #151, #178)

A TMS outage fails every tool call in a conversation, and the customer tries three times. OLT gets one escalation for that conversation, listing each trigger, rather than one per failed message. Once a record has been delivered, a later trigger opens a new one.

**Why this priority:** One customer is owed one callback. Duplicate records would multiply the follow-up work.

**Independent Test:** Run three failing turns in one session and a fourth in another session, then count documents and `triggers` entries.

**Acceptance Scenarios:**

1. **Given** three failing turns in one session with no worker tick between them, **When** each flushes, **Then** exactly one document exists with three entries in its `triggers` array.
2. **Given** a further failing turn in a different session, **When** it flushes, **Then** a second document exists.
3. **Given** a TMS call that returned `503` and a budget that then ran out, **When** the turn flushes, **Then** exactly one document's `triggers` contains both `tms_unavailable` and `tool_budget_exhausted`.
4. **Given** a record whose `delivery.state` is `delivered`, **When** a new trigger arrives in the same session, **Then** a second document is opened and a second POST follows.

### User Story 6 - OLT's webhook is told about an escalation (Priority: P2, #39, #196)

A conversation escalates. After the turn ends, the worker POSTs a small pointer payload to OLT's configured webhook. The customer's turn does not wait for it. When the deployment has a view base URL configured, the payload also carries a link to the conversation.

**Why this priority:** It is the first time an escalation reaches anyone outside the database. It waits on `KU-14` for a real destination.

**Independent Test:** Flush one escalation, tick the worker against a fixture server, and compare the received body with the payload using `toEqual`, once with `CONVERSATION_VIEW_BASE_URL` unset and once with it set.

**support-conversation-data-flow-record** (memory): ## Support Conversation Data Flow Record

Data flow record for the OLT support agent conversation data, per GDPR Article 30.

### Escalation hop (updated by issue #24)

**Previous status:** unmapped destination — the escalation hand-off was listed as a destination with no named store and no retention period.

**Current status (as of #24):** named store with retention period.

- **Store:** `escalations` collection in MongoDB (same instance as `conversations`)
- **Fields:** `sessionId`, `userId`, `trigger`, `occurredAt`, `updatedAt` — pointer fields only, no conversation content
- **Retention period:** same period as the `conversations` collection (set by the data-flow record; this issue does not decide the period)
- **Recipient:** undecided — KU-14 (owner: OLT product contact) determines where the escalation lands; no human is notified by this issue
- **Region:** follows the `conversations` collection's region (decided by `support-agent-deployment` #27)
- **GDPR basis:** same processing basis as the conversation itself (Article 6(1)(b) — performance of contract with the booking customer)
- **Retention sweep:** covered by `support-agent-conversation-persistence` (#23)'s sweep with the same period (CR-002)
- **Erasure:** erasing a conversation by `sessionId` erases its escalation record in the same operation (CR-004)

The notification hop (delivery of the escalation pointer to a configured destination) is a separate data flow added by issue #39 once KU-14 decides the destination.
